Rashi on Pesachim 82b:11:1.hebrew: מעשה חול - שלא נזהרו ונטמאה, נתחללה והוזלה בקדושתה:
Rashi on Pesachim 82b:11:1.english: A secular act - Since they were not careful and it became ritually impure, it became profaned and degraded in its sanctity.

Rashi on Pesachim 82b:11:2.english: And burial should be sufficient for it - to hide it from sight so that dogs do not eat it.

Rashi on Pesachim 82b:12:1.hebrew: מחלוקת - דקאמר תנא קמא פסולו מחמת דבר אחר הוא ובעי עיבור צורה, כגון שנטמאו הבעלים אחר זריקת הדם, דנעשו כל עבודות הדם בהכשר:
Rashi on Pesachim 82b:12:1.english: Dispute - Where the first Tanna says [that] its disqualification is due to another matter and it requires [its] form to decay, [this is] in a case where the owners became ritually impure after the sprinkling of the blood, since all the blood services were performed in a valid manner.

Rashi on Pesachim 82b:12:2.hebrew: אבל נטמאו קודם זריקה - דרחמנא דחייה לפסח שני, נמצאת זריקה שלא בבעלים, וה"ל פסולו בגופו, דזריקה פסולה היא, וישרף מיד בי"ד:
Rashi on Pesachim 82b:12:2.english: But [if] they became ritually impure before the sprinkling - For the Merciful One deferred him to the Second Pesach; [thus,] the sprinkling turns out to be without owners, and it becomes [a case of] its disqualification being in its own body, since it is an invalid sprinkling, and it is burned immediately on the fourteenth [of Nisan].

Rashi on Pesachim 82b:13:1.english: In the blood - For example, [where] the blood became impure or was spilled onto the ground.

Rashi on Pesachim 82b:14:1.hebrew: מחלוקת לפני זריקה - התם פליג ר' יוחנן בן ברוקה, דחשיב ליה פסולו בגופו, ותנא קמא סבר מ"מ לא בא פסול זה אלא מחמת דבר אחר. ורבי יוחנן אמר: אף לאחר זריקה נמי מחלוקת:
Rashi on Pesachim 82b:14:1.english: The dispute [is] before the sprinkling - There, Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka disagrees, for he considers it [a case where] its disqualification is in itself, whereas the Tanna Kamma holds [that] in any event, this disqualification came only due to another matter. And Rabbi Yochanan said: Even after the sprinkling [it is] also a dispute.

Rashi on Pesachim 82b:17:1.hebrew: מפני אנינות נשרפה - חטאת דאהרן, שהיו אוננין ואסורין לאכול בקדשים, דכתיב (דברים כ״ו:י״ד) "לא אכלתי באוני ממנו", ואתו קדשים בקל וחומר ממעשר:
Rashi on Pesachim 82b:17:1.english: It was burned due to acute mourning - [This refers to] the sin-offering of Aaron, for they were acute mourners and forbidden to eat of sacred [offerings], as it is written (Deuteronomy 26:14): "I have not eaten of it in my mourning," and sacred [offerings] are derived via a kal vachomer [a fortiori inference] from tithe.

Rashi on Pesachim 82b:17:2.hebrew: לכך נאמר כאלה - ותקראנה אותי כאלה, שאני אונן, והיאך הייתי אוכל קדשים? למשה נצטוה לאמר להם: קחו את המנחה הנותרת מאשי ה' ואכלוה — באנינות, והיה סבור שאף החטאת תאכל באנינות כמנחה. ואמר לו אהרן: שמא לא שמעת אלא במנחה זו, שהיא קדשי שעה — ליום שמיני של מלואים נצטוית אותה מנחה. ואף אני מודה לך בשעיר נחשון ושעיר של יום, דכתיב (ויקרא ט׳:ג׳): ואל בני ישראל תדבר לאמר קחו שעיר עזים לחטאת, שהם קדשי שעה, חובה ליום, ואכילתן [מותר] לאונן. אבל חטאת זו שעיר ר"ח הוא, וקדשי דורות הן, ואסורין לאונן. ור' יהודה פליג עלה התם ואמר: מפני טומאה נשרפה, שנטמאת באונס. והאי כאלה דריש ליה אמאי דקאמר משה לאהרן: שמא מתוך צערך פשעת בה ונטמאת, וקאמר ליה אהרן למשה: כך אני בעיניך, שאני מבזה קדשי קדשים? אלמלי קראוני כאלה וכאלה, לא הייתי מבזה אותן:
Rashi on Pesachim 82b:17:2.english: For this reason it is stated "such as these" - [Aaron meant:] "And things such as these befell me," [meaning] that I am an onen [acute mourner], so how could I eat sacred offerings? To Moses it was commanded to say to them: "Take the meal-offering that remains of the fire-offerings of the Lord and eat it" — [even] in acute mourning; and [Moses] thought that the sin-offering too would be eaten in acute mourning like the meal-offering. And Aaron said to him: Perhaps you only heard [this command] regarding this meal-offering, which is a temporary offering — for the eighth day of the inauguration you were commanded [concerning] that meal-offering. And I also concede to you regarding the goat of Nachshon and the goat of the day, as it is written (Leviticus 9:3): "And to the children of Israel you shall speak, saying: Take a he-goat for a sin-offering," for they are temporary offerings, an obligation for that day, and eating them is [permitted] to an onen. However, this sin-offering is the goat of Rosh Chodesh, and they are offerings for [all] generations, and are forbidden to an onen. And Rabbi Yehudah disagrees with it there and says: It was burned because of ritual impurity, as it became impure through an unavoidable accident. And this [word] "such as these" he expounds as [referring] to what Moses said to Aaron: Perhaps out of your grief you were negligent with it and it became impure; and Aaron said to Moses: Am I so [contemptible] in your eyes that I would treat the most holy offerings with disrespect? Even if things such as these and such as these had befallen me, I would not have treated them with disrespect.

Rashi on Pesachim 82b:18:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן והא אנינות כלאחר זריקה היא - שאפי' מתו נדב ואביהוא לפני זריקה, אין הזריקה נפסלת בכך; דחטאת לא דמיא לפסח דעיקרו לאכילה, דאילו חטאת לא חיישינן לאוכלין דידה, דלכפרה אתיא, ואכל ישראל שהיו ראוין. ואם מפני שהקריבוה באנינות ונפסלה, דאונן שעבד חילל — לא הדיוטים הקריבוה, כי אם אהרן עצמו, וקיימא לן (יומא דף יג:) כהן גדול מקריב אונן ואינו אוכל. והכי אמרינן בזבחים (דף קא.), ודרשינן "הן היום הקריבו", דקאמר ליה משה לאהרן: דילמא באנינות אקריבתיה ופסלתיה, ועל כן שרפתם אותה? א"ל אהרן: "הן היום" — וכי הם היום הקריבו, דפסל בהו אנינות? אני הקרבתי, דלא פסלא בי אנינות, ושריפה מיד הואי בלא עיבור צורה. ומדקאמר ר' יוחנן דר' נחמיה ור' יוחנן בן ברוקה אמרו דבר אחד, אלמא ס"ל דפלוגתא דמתניתין אף כשנטמאו לאחר זריקה, דעבודות דם נעשו בהכשר, ואפילו הכי ישרף מיד מפני שאין מי שיאכלנו, כי חטאת דאהרן לא היה לה פסול אחר אלא שלא היו לה אוכלין. וספרים כתב בהן: "והא אנינות לאחר זריקה הואי". וקשיא לי: מנלן הא? הלא לא נתפרשו בפרשה אלא עבודות של קרבנות שמיני, אבל קרבנות של ר"ח לא נתפרשו בה! ועוד, מדקא מהדר ליה אהרן "וכי הן הקריבו והלא אני הקרבתי", מכלל דקודם זריקה הואי אנינות:
Rashi on Pesachim 82b:18:1.english: This is how we read [the text]: "Now, acute mourning is like [a disqualification] after sprinkling" - For even if Nadav and Avihu died before the sprinkling [of the blood], the sprinkling is not invalidated thereby; for a sin-offering is not comparable to a Paschal offering, whose primary purpose is for eating, whereas [with regard to] a sin-offering, we are not concerned about its eaters, since it comes for atonement, and all Israel [for whom it atoned] were fit. And if [you ask whether it was disqualified] because they offered it while in a state of acute mourning [aninut], since an acute mourner [onen] who performs the service profanes [the offering] — ordinary priests did not offer it, but rather Aaron himself, and it is established for us (Yoma 13b) [that] a High Priest offers [sacrifices] while an acute mourner, though he does not eat [of them]. And so we say in Zevachim (101a), where we expound [the verse] "Behold, this day they offered" (Leviticus 10:19): Moses said to Aaron: "Perhaps you offered it in a state of acute mourning and invalidated it, and therefore you burned it?" Aaron said to him: "'Behold, this day' — did they [my sons] offer [it] today, to whom acute mourning is a disqualification? I offered [it], to whom acute mourning is not a disqualification!" And the burning took place immediately, without waiting for [the meat's] appearance to become disfigured [ibbur tzurah]. And since Rabbi Yochanan says that Rabbi Nehemiah and Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka said the same thing, evidently he holds that the dispute in our Mishnah [applies] even when [the offerings] became impure after the sprinkling, where the blood services were performed validly, and even so it must be burned immediately because there is no one to eat it — for Aaron's sin-offering had no other disqualification except that it had no eaters. And [some] manuscripts have written in them: "Now, the acute mourning was after the sprinkling." But this is difficult for me: from where do we [know] this? Were not only the services of the eighth-day [inauguration] offerings detailed in the Torah portion, whereas the Rosh Chodesh offerings were not detailed in it! Furthermore, since Aaron replied to him, "Did they offer [it]? Did I not offer [it]?" — this implies that the acute mourning occurred before the sprinkling.

Rashi on Pesachim 82b:1:1.english: Its blood was spilled - For there is no sprinkling [of the blood] here, and the meat was not permitted [to be eaten].

Rashi on Pesachim 82b:1:2.hebrew: וכן יצא דמה - דמהאי פנימה דלעיל נפקא, דמיפסיל אף הדם ביציאה:
Rashi on Pesachim 82b:1:2.english: And similarly, [if] its blood was taken out - For it is derived from that [word] "inside" [mentioned] above that the blood also becomes disqualified through leaving [the courtyard].

Rashi on Pesachim 82b:1:3.hebrew: דקיימא לן דכל הני בשריפה - בכל הגמרא אנו מוצאין בכל פסולי קדשים יצאו לבית השריפה, ומנלן מקרא:
Rashi on Pesachim 82b:1:3.english: We maintain that all of these [must be] burned - Throughout the Gemara we find regarding all disqualified consecrated [offerings] [that] they go out to the place of burning, and from where do we [derive] this from Scripture?

Rashi on Pesachim 82b:2:1.english: In the sacred place - In the [Temple] courtyard.

Rashi on Pesachim 82b:3:1.hebrew: פסולי שאר קדשים - שמחיצתן בכשרותן בעזרה, דכתיב בהן (ויקרא ו׳:ט׳) ״בחצר אהל מועד״, ואימורי קדשים קלים שנפסלו — דבכשרותן היתה חומת העזרה מחיצתה, דהא הקטרה בעו — מנין שאף כשנפסלו תהא שם שריפתן? ולהכי נקט אימורים, דאי ניטמא בשרן של קדשים קלים, דנאכל בכל העיר, שריפתן נמי בכל העיר, כדתנן: ״שורפין אותו בחצרותיהן או על גגותיהן״:
Rashi on Pesachim 82b:3:1.english: Disqualified [ones] of other sacred [offerings] - Whose boundary when valid is in the Courtyard, as it is written concerning them (Leviticus 6:9): "in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting," and the sacrificial portions of offerings of lesser sanctity that became disqualified — for when valid, the wall of the Courtyard was their boundary, since they require burning [on the altar] — from where [do we derive] that even when they became disqualified, their burning should be there? And for this reason [the Gemara] mentioned sacrificial portions: for if the meat of offerings of lesser sanctity became ritually impure, which is eaten anywhere in the city [of Jerusalem], their burning is likewise anywhere in the city, as we learned [in a Mishnah]: "they burn it in their courtyards or on their roofs."

Rashi on Pesachim 82b:3:2.hebrew: קדשים קלים - דבעי שריפה כלל בשאר פסולין חוץ מטומאה, מנלן? ומטומאה ליכא למילף, דשאני טומאה דפסלה אף בתרומה ומעשר:
Rashi on Pesachim 82b:3:2.english: Offerings of lesser sanctity - [That] they require burning at all in [the case of] other disqualifications besides ritual impurity, from where [do we know this]? And from ritual impurity it cannot be derived, for ritual impurity is different, as it disqualifies even terumah and tithe.

Rashi on Pesachim 82b:4:1.hebrew: הלכתא גמירי לה - וחטאת דאהרן לא איצטריכא לפרושי בה שריפה באנינותה וביציאתה, אלא מעשה שהיה הוא דאישתעי. ולקמן פריך: והבשר אשר יגע בכל טמא למה לי:
Rashi on Pesachim 82b:4:1.english: It is a law learned as a tradition - And [as for] the sin-offering of Aaron, it was not necessary to specify burning in its case [whether] due to its [association with] mourning [aninut] or its leaving [the Courtyard]; rather, it is [simply] recounting an incident that took place. And later [the Gemara] asks: Why do I need [the verse], "And the flesh that touches any impure thing"?

Rashi on Pesachim 82b:5:1.hebrew: אפי' פיגול - שפסולו בגופו, טעון עיבור צורה. והא דתנא דרבה בר אבוה לא איתפרש מהיכא:
Rashi on Pesachim 82b:5:1.english: Even piggul - whose disqualification is in its own body, requires decay of form. And this [statement] of the tanna of Rabbah bar Avuh was not explained from where [it is].

Rashi on Pesachim 82b:5:2.hebrew: מנא ליה - דבעי עיבור צורה? פשיטא לן דטעמא משום דגמר "עון" "עון" מנותר: כתיב בפיגול (שם ז) "והנפש האוכלת ממנו עונה תשא", וכתיב בנותר (שם יט) "ואוכליו עונו ישא". והאי קרא בנותר מוקמינן ליה בכריתות (דף ה.) בגזרה שוה: כתיב "כי את קודש ה' חילל", וכתיב "ושרפת את הנותר באש לא יאכל כי קודש הוא". וגמר פיגול מנותר: מה נותר כבר עובר צורתו, אף פיגול צריך שתעובר צורתו. ואדגמר מנותר, ליגמרי' מחטאת דאהרן שנשרפה בו ביום, דכתיב ביה נמי עון: "ואותה נתן לכם לשאת את עון העדה", ומשה הודה להם, דכתיב "וייטב בעיניו":
Rashi on Pesachim 82b:5:2.english: From where does he [derive] - that it requires decay of form? It is obvious to us that the reason is because he derives [a gezerah shavah of] "iniquity" (avon) [and] "iniquity" (avon) from notar: it is written regarding piggul (there, [Leviticus] 7), "And the soul that eats of it shall bear its iniquity," and it is written regarding notar (there, [Leviticus] 19), "And those who eat it shall bear his iniquity." And this verse regarding notar, we establish it in Keritot (5a) through a gezerah shavah: it is written, "for he has profaned the sacred [offering] of the Lord" [Leviticus 19:8], and it is written, "and you shall burn the remainder (notar) with fire; it shall not be eaten, for it is sacred" [Exodus 29:34]. And he derives piggul from notar: just as notar has already undergone decay of its form, so too piggul must have its form decay. And instead of deriving [it] from notar, let him derive it from the sin-offering of Aaron, which was burned on that very day, about which "iniquity" is also written: "and He has given it to you to bear the iniquity of the congregation" [Leviticus 10:17], and Moses agreed with them, as it is written: "and it was good in his eyes" [Leviticus 10:20].

Rashi on Pesachim 82b:7:1.hebrew: כי האי גוונא - בין למאן דאמר בזבחים מפני אנינות נשרפה, בין למאן דאמר מפני טומאה נשרפה, לדורות בעיא עיבור צורה. והוראת שעה היתה ששרפוה לבו ביום:
Rashi on Pesachim 82b:7:1.english: In a case like this - Whether according to the one who says in [tractate] Zevachim [that] it was burned because of acute mourning [aninut], or according to the one who says [that] it was burned because of ritual impurity, for [future] generations it would require decay of form. And it was a provisional edict that they burned it on that very day.

Rashi on Pesachim 82b:8:1.english: That their burning [must be] in the sacred [place] - That one must burn them in the [Temple] courtyard.

Tosafot on Pesachim 82b:11:1.hebrew: אבל נטמא דאיתיה בחולין כו' - תימה לרשב"א: ניליף כולהו מטמא, ואמאי צריך הלכתא? ואומר ר"י דה"א: מה שנוהג בחולין הוי חומרא, הואיל ומעשה חול אתעביד ביה. וא"ת: ונילף קל וחומר מתרומה דבעי שריפה? וי"ל: דאיכא למיפרך — מה לתרומה דאסורה לזרים, תאמר בקדשים קלים דשרי. רשב"א:
Tosafot on Pesachim 82b:11:1.english: "But if it became ritually impure, which applies to unconsecrated [meat], etc." - Rashba is perplexed: Let us derive all of them [the other disqualifications] from [the case of] one that became ritually impure, and why is a special teaching needed [for them]? And Ri says that I might have thought that [the fact] that it applies to unconsecrated items is a stringency, since a mundane act was done to it. And if you say: Let us derive [that a ritually impure offering requires burning] via an a fortiori inference from terumah, which requires burning? One can answer: Because one can refute [that inference]: What [is unique] to terumah is that it is forbidden to non-priests; will you say [the same] regarding offerings of lesser sanctity, which are permitted [to non-priests]? (Rashba.)

Tosafot on Pesachim 82b:16:1.hebrew: לאחר זריקה מחלוקת - פירוש: אף לאחר זריקה; דאי דוקא, "בדם ובבעלים" מאן קתני לה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 82b:16:1.english: After sprinkling [there is] a dispute - Explanation: [this means] even after sprinkling; for if [it meant] specifically [after sprinkling], who taught [the baraita stating] "regarding the blood or the owners"?

Tosafot on Pesachim 82b:16:2.hebrew: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה ורבי נחמיה אמרו דבר אחד - וא"ת: דילמא לעולם רבי נחמיה כרבנן ס"ל דבעו עיבור צורה, וחטאת אהרן שנשרף מיד מפני אנינות — הוראת שעה היתה, דעדיין לא פירש להם עיבור צורה, כדפירש בקונטרס! ואומר רשב"א, דלפי מה שפירש ר"י דסברא דפסול בעלים בעי עיבור צורה — אתי שפיר; דהכא לא שייך "הוראת שעה היתה", דאנינות הוי פסול בעלים, ומסברא בעי עיבור צורה. ולעיל דקאמר "הוראת שעה היתה", קסבר דמפני טומאה נשרפה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 82b:16:2.english: "Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka and Rabbi Neḥemya said the same thing" - And if you ask: Perhaps Rabbi Neḥemya actually holds like the Rabbis, who require decay of form [before burning disqualified sacrificial meat], and Aaron's sin-offering, which was burned immediately because of aninut [acute mourning], was a temporary ruling [hora'at sha'ah], since decay of form had not yet been explained to them, as Rashi explained! The Rashba says that according to what the R"I explained — that it is logical that a disqualification of the owners requires decay of form — it works out well; for here, [saying] "it was a temporary ruling" does not apply, since aninut is a disqualification of the owners and by logic requires decay of form. Whereas above, where [the Gemara] said "it was a temporary ruling," it held that [the sin-offering] was burned because of ritual impurity [tumah].

Tosafot on Pesachim 82b:7:1.hebrew: ונגמר עון עון מחטאת דאהרן - תימה לרשב"א: א"כ, לישתוק מעון דפיגול וממילא נימא דישרף מיד? וי"ל דבלאו הכי איצטריך למיכתב עון בפיגול, דבפרק שני דזבחים (דף כח:) יליף בפיגול כרת — עון עון מנותר:
Tosafot on Pesachim 82b:7:1.english: And let us derive "iniquity" [and] "iniquity" from the sin-offering of Aaron - This is puzzling to the Rashba: if so, let [the Torah] be silent about "iniquity" regarding piggul, and automatically we would say that it should be burned immediately? And one can answer that even without this, it was necessary to write "iniquity" regarding piggul, because in the second chapter of Zevachim (28b) [the Gemara] derives karet for piggul [via the verbal analogy of] "iniquity" [and] "iniquity" from notar.
